asr.transcript: A serial killer asked the police one question. "It'll flop you disc betraced?" They told him it was safe. They lied. From 1974, a killer who called himself BTK murdered ten people in and around Wichita, Kansas. He taunted police and the press with letters. Then for years silence. In 2004, he started writing again. In January 2005, he left a note inside a cereal box. "Can I communicate with floppy and not be traced to a computer?" "If it was safe," he said, "answer with an ad in the newspaper." Police ran the ad. Rex, it will be okay. Weeks later, a television station received a floppy disk from BTK. Examiners found one deleted file. Hidden in its data. Christ Luther in church. And the name, Dennis. The president of that church's council was Dennis Rader. The day in a test confirmed the link. On February 25th, 2005, he was arrested. He pleaded guilty to all 10 murders. 10 consecutive life sentences. 31 years of hiding, ended by one question, one lie, and one deleted file. (soft music)
